header: Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jordan Li (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Seabright), Marco Ruiz (Seabright), Priya Singh (Seabright)
summary: Discovery focused on embeddings + reranking architecture. Customer currently uses a hybrid search (BM25 + Pinecone) and is evaluating replacing Pinecone with Redwood-hosted embeddings + reranker for lower latency and better relevance. Main concerns: throughput (QPS), embedding dimensionality, vector DB integration patterns (hosted vs dedicated vs private), security (VPC/KMS/SOC2), and rerank cost using cross-encoders. Agreed next steps: share benchmarks, pricing bands, schedule private deployment deep-dive.
topics: vector DB integration patterns (hosted vector store vs customer-managed DB)
throughput and latency SLOs, batching strategies
hybrid search (BM25 + ANN) and reranker placement
transcript: [00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, can you hear me okay?
[00:05] Priya: Yep, loud and clear. Thanks Maya. Lena, Marco thanks for making time.
[00:12] Lena: Yeah, thanks. Quick agenda from our side is: show you our current setup, talk about latency pain, and see how Redwood might fit for embeddings + rerank.
[00:25] Jordan: Great, we'll do a quick intro to Redwood's hosting options and then deep dive on embeddings/throughput. Feel free to interrupt with questions we'll ask about QPS and cost early on.

[01:10] Marco: To give context, we run user search over ~1.2M documents, currently using BM25 first-pass and Pinecone for ANN, then a cross-encoder reranker on the top 50. Typical peak QPS is 120, but spiky sometimes 300 for short bursts during launches.
[01:48] Maya: Nice, that helps. Are you using 1536-dimension embeddings today?
[01:53] Marco: Yes, we're using a 1536 OpenAI-style embedding, roughly 1.5k dims, costy but we liked recall. We're exploring smaller dims to cut storage/costs if the reranker can compensate.

[02:22] Jordan: OK. Two patterns we see: 1) keep 1536 embeddings for recall and do ANN in a hosted vector DB, 2) use lower-dim (512) for the first-pass and rely on a cross-encoder rerank to recover precision. Both map to different cost/perf tradeoffs.
[02:45] Lena: For us latency is pretty important search results need to return under 200ms for the main product flow, or conversion drops. So the reranker in the critical path is tricky.

[03:08] Jordan: Understood. Our Hosted API supports prefix caching and streaming; for rerank-heavy workloads teams often run the ANN in-hosted mode (Redwood handles KV/ANN) and the cross-encoder on Dedicated or Private if you want VPC isolation and lower P99. We can also do hybrid: Redwood provides embeddings + ANN, and you keep your Pinecone if you want to test incrementally.
[03:47] Marco: How would the reranker look cost-wise? If we run a cross-encoder over top 50 per query at 120 QPS that's a lot of inference.

[04:02] Jordan: Right. Typical approach is to reduce the candidate set via ANN to 10-20 and run smaller cross-encoders or cheaper distillation models for rerank. Or you can run the cross-encoder asynchronously for freshness and use a faster embed-based re-ranker for real-time.
[04:35] Priya: We're also very sensitive on data residency and audit logs. Any details on Private deployment?

[04:43] Maya: Yes Private gives you a control plane in your VPC and optional on-prem. We integrate with customer KMS/HSM and provide audit logs; we have SOC2 documentation which Jordan will share. There's also a Dedicated option (reserved GPU pools) if you want predictable throughput without managing infra.
[05:10] Lena: Can you share latency numbers for 512 vs 1536 embeddings for ANN lookup? We're trying to model end-to-end p95.

[05:20] Jordan: We have benchmark spreadsheets I'll upload our benchmark that shows vector lookup latencies across dims on A100 and on Multi-GPU dedicated nodes. Rough ballpark: ANN (HNSW) 1536 dim lookup ~3-8ms per query at scale on optimized nodes; 512 dims can be ~1.5-4ms. But throughput and memory tradeoffs matter 1536 increases index size ~3x.
[06:05] Marco: Index size is a big deal. We pay Pinecone storage costs today. If Redwood-hosted reduces storage/operation cost that's compelling.
[06:18] Maya: Also note our smart batching and prefix/KV caching reduce per-token costs and number of cross-encoder calls when you cache user session prefixes.
[06:40] Lena: What about hybrid search BM25 + ANN? We still want lexical for certain queries.

[06:48] Jordan: Totally supported. Customers often do BM25 first, then embed top 200 results and merge with ANN results, then rerank. Redwood's routing can do policy-based merging. Some minor OCR/transcription mismatches in infra docs, but we'll share an example flow.
[07:20] Priya: Security wise, we need SAML SSO, RBAC, audit logs, and KMS. Also, do you allow bringing your own vector DB if we want?

[07:30] Maya: Yes, you can either use Redwood's hosted vector store or point Redwood to your managed DB (e.g., Pinecone/Milvus) via connectors. For Private, you can host the vector index inside the VPC no egress.
[08:02] Marco: Do you support approximate nearest neighbor libraries other than HNSW? We experiment with IVF-PQ for lower memory.

[08:10] Jordan: We support multiple ANN backends; the runtime picks the best kernels. For high-dim at scale we sometimes use quantized IVF-PQ combos to shrink indexes with minimal recall loss; we'll include recommended quantization profiles.
[08:40] Lena: Great. Pricing: we'd like to see hosted per-token/embedding pricing vs Dedicated reserved-monthly and what a pilot would cost.

[08:50] Maya: I'll send a pricing band. Quick note: Dedicated has commit tiers and predictable throughput; Private has a one-time platform fee plus support. We'll include sample pricing for your baseline QPS of 120 and for spikes to 300.
[09:20] Marco: For throughput, what are recommended batch sizes? We batch embeddings requests in our pipeline right now but in production it's hard to batch cross-encoder calls.

[09:31] Jordan: For embedding generation, batching is effective batching 16-64 depending on model gives throughput wins. For cross-encoder rerank, you'd want smaller batches to meet latency SLOs. Redwood's serving runtime supports dynamic batching with latency constraints.
[10:05] Priya: On integration, what does a typical pilot look like? Do we push docs to Redwood or keep them in our DB and call API?

[10:14] Maya: Either works. Common pilot: we ingest a subset (100k) into Redwood-hosted vector store to run benchmarks. Alternatively we point Redwood at customer index for a read-only pilot. We recommended the subset approach for apples-to-apples comparisons.
[10:40] Lena: If we do a pilot, can you run a live RPS test against our realistic query set?
[10:48] Jordan: Yes if you share the query set we'll run a Redwood-hosted benchmark (QPS, p50/p95 latencies, recall metrics). We'll also test hybrid scenarios.
[11:20] Marco: A couple of nitty-gritty: what embedding metrics should we track? We track recall@10/50, MRR, and latency. Any Redwood-specific telemetry?
[11:30] Jordan: Redwood Console gives token-level cost, per-route latency, per-model breakdowns, tracing hooks, and error analysis. You can hook your dashboards to our traces.
[12:00] Lena: One concern: moving to high-dim embeddings increases storage and query cost, but reduces rerank load. Any guidance on target dims?

[12:10] Jordan: For many customers, 512-768 dims with a strong reranker hits a sweet spot. If you prioritize pure recall and want minimal reranker calls, 1536 is safer. We'll recommend tests: run 512 and 1536 on your sample corpus and measure recall/latency tradeoffs.
[12:50] Priya: For Private deployment, what's the timeline to get infra stood up?
[12:57] Maya: For VPC-based Private, typical timeline is 4-8 weeks depending on approvals and network setup. Dedicated is faster often 2-3 weeks once contracts are signed.
[13:18] Marco: Any known integration issues with our stack? We're on AWS, Kubernetes, and Postgres for metadata.

[13:25] Jordan: That's a common stack. We have connectors for S3/GCS ingestion, and our private control plane connects over VPC peering or private link. For metadata, we can push to Postgres or keep in Redwood's metadata store.
[14:05] Lena: Can you give an example end-to-end latency estimate: ANN lookup + cross-encoder rerank for p95 in a Dedicated setup?

[14:15] Jordan: Rough example: ANN lookup (10 candidates) 5ms, data marshalling 2ms, cross-encoder (small distil cross-encoder) 30-60ms depending on model, total ~40-70ms p95 in optimized Dedicated infra. If running a heavier cross-encoder p95 can jump to 150-250ms.
[15:00] Priya: That's promising. We need to ensure p95 under 200ms, so a distil reranker or fewer candidates might be needed.
[15:12] Maya: Agreed also look at caching top queries and using a lightweight re-ranker in-path with async heavy re-ranker for quality metrics.
[16:00] Marco: About vector DB migration: if we move from Pinecone to Redwood hosted store, is there a bulk export/import?

[16:10] Jordan: Yes we provide migration tooling and support. We can bulk ingest via S3 or stream changes for sync. For large corpora we recommend initial bulk load into Redwood then incremental sync.
[16:45] Lena: Any gotchas with quantization and recall? We tried 8-bit quantization and saw recall drop for certain entity-heavy queries.

[16:53] Jordan: Quantization can affect certain query types. We'll share quantization profiles: per-corpus tuning some corpora work well with PQ, others need hybrid IVF+HNSW. We'll include examples in the benchmark sheet.
[17:25] Priya: Can Redwood handle A/B experiments for reranker models? We want to test multiple rerankers in prod.
[17:32] Maya: Yes Console supports rollouts, canary deploys, A/B tests, and automatic fallback policies. You can route a percentage of traffic to different rerankers.
[18:05] Marco: On monitoring do you provide per-query traces to map which stage adds latency?
[18:12] Jordan: Yes. Tracing hooks show per-route/model latencies and token-level breakdowns. You can also export traces to your observability stack.
[19:00] Lena: Let's talk about legal/procurement: are there standard NDs and data processing addenda?
[19:08] Maya: Yes we have standard DPA and DPA addendum. For Private there's additional clauses. I'll attach the legal pack.
[19:40] Marco: Is there a sandbox or trial credits for us to validate before a contract?
[19:45] Maya: We provide trial credits for Hosted and a pilot pricing for Dedicated. For Private we usually do a scoped POC which is priced separately.
[20:10] Priya: Excellent. We're also evaluating Milvus for self-host, and Pinecone for hosted; curious how Redwood compares on ops/observability.

[20:18] Jordan: Compared to self-hosted Milvus, Redwood reduces ops burden and provides production-grade observability. Compared to Pinecone, we offer tighter integration with rerankers and Private/Dedicated options with VPC/KMS for compliance.
[21:00] Lena: Any references or case studies for similar customers?
[21:05] Maya: We'll share a case study where a retail customer cut reranker costs by 40% by moving to 512 dims + optimized reranker and using Redwood Dedicated.
[21:35] Marco: One final technical: can we run cross-encoder on CPU for cost reasons?
[21:42] Jordan: You can, but latency will be higher. We typically recommend GPU for cross-encoders for p95 SLOs. Lower-cost options are distil-models on cheaper GPUs.
[22:05] Maya: We're going to attach the benchmark sheet and sample configs after this call.
[22:18] Jordan: I'll also include recommended index types and quantization profiles for your corpus size.
[22:45] Marco: Timeline-wise if we want a pilot next month, what do you need from us?
[22:53] Maya: Sample corpus (100k), query set, and expected QPS profile. We'll provision a pilot cluster and run benchmarks. Jordan will run the tests and we'll present results.
[23:25] Priya: That works. Any initial blockers?
[23:31] Jordan: Network/firewall for VPC peering could add time for Private. Otherwise the main work is data prep.
[24:00] Lena: Can you email the SOC2 + KMS integration guide?
[24:05] Maya: Yup I'll include that. Expect it in the next 24-48 hours.
[24:30] Marco: How do you handle model upgrades for rerankers do you version-run?
[24:37] Jordan: Console supports model versioning and rollouts with automatic fallback. You can specify percentage traffic and we keep tracing per-version.
[25:10] Lena: Ok let's recap next steps I'll list what we'll provide and what we expect from Redwood.
[25:20] Lena: We'll send sample queries, 100k doc subset, and our latency targets. Marco and I will align internally on stakeholders.
[25:35] Maya: Great. To recap Redwood action items: pricing, benchmark sheet, SOC2 + KMS docs, pilot provisioning steps.
[26:00] Priya: Sounds good. Anything else?
[26:05] Jordan: One small note if you want to keep Pinecone during a staged migration, Redwood connectors let you run dual-read for comparison.
[26:20] Marco: Helpful. We'll likely try a dual-read pilot first.
[26:40] Lena: Thanks everyone this was useful. We'll review internally and get back on scheduling the technical demo.
[26:48] Maya: Thanks all I'll follow up with the materials and a proposed time for the demo week of Oct 4.
[26:55] Priya: Thanks, bye.
[27:00] (call ends)
